title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Tampa, FL: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Tampa Bay welders and QC staff: study online or train on site. Ship repair, steel, bridge and plant codes covered. Get a quote.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Tampa, Florida: A Six-Day Course for Tampa Bay Welders and Inspectors
html:
Tampa Bay keeps welders busy in more trades than most metro areas its size: ship repair yards on the port channels, structural steel for a growing skyline, bridge and highway steel, fuel and bulk terminals, and the phosphate and power plants that ring the bay. All of those employers need people who can judge a weld against a code and sign for it. Atlantis NDT prepares Tampa candidates for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination with a six-day (6-day) course. Individuals study online with an instructor answering their questions, and a Tampa Bay employer can bring the full six days to its own shop, yard or plant for a group of its people. The American Welding Society (AWS) administers the CWI exam and issues the certification. Atlantis prepares candidates, certifies no one, and has no classroom or office in Tampa. To start, request a Tampa CWI exam prep quote.

What drives CWI demand around Tampa Bay

Tampa is not a one-industry town, and its welding work is spread across sectors that answer to different codes. An inspector here might check structural connections on a downtown tower one month, piping at a fertilizer or power plant during an outage the next, and a barge in drydock after that. Local employers value inspectors who can move between codes, yet the AWS exam asks each candidate to pick one code book for Part C. Choosing it with the Tampa market in mind is one of the more useful decisions a local candidate makes, and the sections below walk through where the work is and which code each part of it follows.

Demand also comes from paperwork, not just welding. Customers, building officials, transportation agencies and plant owners increasingly ask contractors to show who inspected the welding and on what credential. A fabricator that cannot name a qualified inspector on its quality plan can lose bids, so CWIs are hired for the documents they can sign as much as for what they can see.

Ship repair and marine fabrication on the port

Port Tampa Bay is home to working commercial ship repair. Tampa Ship, LLC operates at Port Tampa Bay with three large dry docks and handles repair and conversion work on large hulls, tugs, barges and offshore units. Gulf Marine Repair, on Grant Street, does dry-dock maintenance and repair for barges, articulated tug-barge units and other heavy commercial vessels. Hendry Corporation, a shipbuilding and repair company at Port Hendry in the Port of Tampa, built a 2,500-ton drydock on its own site in 2014 with help from a federal Small Shipyard grant administered by MARAD. On the leisure side, Lazzara Yachts builds and refits composite and metal yachts in Tampa.

Repair welding on a ship answers to the vessel's classification society rules, the owner's repair specification and, for government vessels, the contracting agency's welding requirements, rather than to one AWS code. The inspection tasks are familiar all the same: confirming fit-up and joint preparation on inserts and doublers, checking that welders hold the right qualifications for position and thickness, watching preheat on thicker or higher-strength plate, and accepting finished welds for size, profile and surface defects. In the yards, welding inspectors work next to NDT technicians running ultrasonic thickness surveys on hull plating, magnetic particle testing on structural welds and penetrant testing on stainless piping. The CWI exam offers no marine code, so a candidate from the yards will usually find AWS D1.1's structural steel provisions the closest fit to hull, deck and frame work.

Structural steel and the building market

Construction is the other big employer of welding inspectors in Tampa. Office and residential towers, hotels, hospitals, parking structures, warehouses and industrial buildings around Hillsborough and Pinellas counties use structural steel that is fabricated and erected to AWS D1.1. The project specification and inspection plan say who verifies the welding, in the shop and in the field, and how that verification is recorded. Fabricators that hold or pursue AISC certification must show a working quality system with qualified welding inspection, and many of them meet that with a CWI on staff.

Florida adds its own layer. The state's threshold building program puts a licensed special inspector in charge of structural inspection on larger buildings, and where that plan calls for structural welding verification, the hands-on checks are often done by a certified welding inspector working for the testing firm or the fabricator. For a Tampa candidate in building construction, that means the CWI is often the credential that gets your name onto the inspection report.

Bridges, highways and heavy civil steel

Bridge and highway work brings a second structural code into play. The new Howard Frankland Bridge span across Old Tampa Bay, a Florida Department of Transportation project, opened to traffic in March 2025, and widening and interchange projects around the bay keep highway steel moving through regional fabrication shops. Steel bridge members are welded to AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code, and transportation agencies expect qualified inspection and full documentation on that work. Bridge fabrication also tends to involve tighter controls than building work on preheat, welder qualification and nondestructive testing of main members. If your employer fabricates bridge girders or other bridge steel, D1.5 is the Part C choice worth considering, because it is the book you will be applying every day.

Phosphate, power and fuel terminals

East and south of the city, phosphate mining and fertilizer production across Polk and Hillsborough counties support large chemical plants with acid units, storage tanks, slurry lines and process piping that need welded repair during planned outages. Utility power stations around the bay add boiler tube, piping and structural welding, and the fuel and bulk terminals at Port Tampa Bay bring tank, pipeline and loading-system work. Corrosive service in the fertilizer plants means stainless and alloy welding is common, and outage schedules mean inspectors are needed in bursts.

Plant welding is usually inspected against ASME or API documents rather than structural codes: ASME B31.3 for process piping, ASME B31.1 for power piping, ASME Section IX for procedure and welder qualification, and API 1104 for pipeline welding into and out of terminals. AWS offers an ASME option for Part C that covers Section IX together with B31.1 and B31.3, which suits a candidate whose work is mostly plant shutdowns. In-service inspection of tanks and pressure vessels is a separate field run by API 653 and API 510 certified inspectors; Atlantis does not train for those certifications, but CWIs regularly work beside API inspectors on the repair welding those inspections call for.

The AWS Florida West Coast Section

AWS organizes its members into local sections, and the Tampa Bay area falls under the AWS Florida West Coast Section. The section's members sit on welding advisory committee boards for schools in Hillsborough, Pinellas, Manatee, Polk and Lee counties, so it has close ties to the region's welding programs. Section meetings and events are a practical way for a CWI candidate to meet working inspectors, ask how local employers use the credential, and hear about AWS activity in Florida. Its current calendar is posted on the section's pages at sections.aws.org.

Joining AWS is separate from taking the exam, but members pay lower AWS examination fees according to the AWS fee table, and section contacts can be a good source of advice on which code book local employers prefer.

Welding programs that feed the Tampa Bay workforce

Many CWI candidates begin as welders, and the Tampa Bay area trains a steady stream of them. Schools whose welding advisory boards include Florida West Coast Section representatives include:

  • Hillsborough Community College, Hillsborough County
  • Erwin Technical College, Hillsborough County
  • Tampa Bay Technical High School, East Bay High School and Jefferson High School, Hillsborough County
  • Pinellas Technical College, with campuses in Clearwater and St. Petersburg, Pinellas County
  • Manatee Technical Institute, Manatee County
  • Travis Technical College, Polk County

A technical college welding certificate does not shorten the road to CWI as much as graduates hope. AWS credits completed trade or vocational courses with one year of substitution, which still leaves four years of welding-related work, while a high school diploma alone means five. Graduates in a hurry to inspect can look first at the AWS Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI) credential, which asks for less experience, and move up to the CWI exam once they qualify. Program details belong to each school; they are named here because they appear on the section's advisory board list.

Where Tampa candidates sit the exam

The CWI exam happens in two kinds of place. Part A (Fundamentals) and Part C (Code Application) are computer-based and taken at a Prometric test center; AWS reports more than 100 Prometric centers in the United States, and Prometric's own site will show you the nearest ones to Tampa. Part B, the practical, is run by AWS itself at its seminar and exam locations. AWS lists Tampa among its CWI training locations, but when we checked in November 2026 its Tampa page showed no upcoming seminars for Florida, so a Tampa candidate should be ready to travel for the practical.

Plan backward from the practical. Look at the AWS Seminar and Exam Schedule early, choose a Part B date you can reach, and then book the Prometric parts within the order and window your AWS confirmation letter sets. Remember the visual acuity record: AWS limits how old the eye examination can be on exam day, so schedule it with your local eye doctor once your dates are firm.

Choosing a Part C code book as a Tampa candidate

Your Tampa Bay workCode book to consider
Building and structural steel fabrication or erectionAWS D1.1
Steel bridge fabrication for FDOT or other ownersAWS D1.5
Pipelines, terminal pipe runs and gas utility workAPI 1104
Power, fertilizer and process plant pipingASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3
Ship repair and marine steel fabricationAWS D1.1 (no marine code is offered)
Aluminum structures, railings and marine aluminumAWS D1.2

Whichever book you pick, study the edition AWS lists for the exam, which can be older than the copy in your shop. The current options and editions are on the national AWS CWI exam prep page, and the site's guides to AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5 and API 1104 give background on each.

How the six-day course works in Tampa

The six days run in one sequence. Two days cover Fundamentals: processes, terms, joint design and symbols, then metallurgy, testing, discontinuities, safety and fabrication math. Day three is practical measurement and document work for Part B. Day four is spent inside your chosen code book for Part C. Day five is timed practice papers, and day six is review of weak areas plus exam logistics and the AWS documents checklist. The full outline is on the national page.

Individual candidates in Tampa study online with a study plan, course materials, original practice questions written to the AWS topic areas, and timed papers, with an instructor answering questions by message. Nothing is scheduled at a fixed time, which suits rotating shifts at a yard or a plant outage.

A Tampa Bay employer can bring the course to its own site, whether that is a fabrication shop, a yard on the port channel or a plant in Polk County. On-site groups practise Part B on their own welds with their own fillet, bridge cam and undercut gauges, and Part C in the code their work follows. Atlantis does not ship replica kits; the shop's real joints make honest practice material. Each person still applies to AWS individually and must meet its eligibility and vision rules.

From CWI into NDT and inspection work in Tampa

Yards and plants like one person who can judge a weld by eye and then test it, so many inspectors pair the CWI with NDT qualifications. Atlantis runs ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Tampa candidates, online with practicals at the employer's facility, and the employer certifies its people under its written practice; see NDT training in Tampa, NDT training in Florida and VT Level 2 training. Atlantis also sends technicians to Tampa Bay sites for weld inspection and visual testing using UT, MT, PT and VT. Between study sessions, the Practical NDT welding workshop lets you rehearse inspection steps in a browser.

Budgeting and requesting a Tampa quote

AWS publishes its current CWI examination and seminar fees on aws.org, and the CWI exam budget planner helps you add travel for the practical and the code book. For the course, tell us whether it is for you or a group, how many candidates, each person's education and welding experience in outline, the code book each plans to choose and, for on-site delivery, where your Tampa Bay facility is and which weeks suit production. Send your Tampa CWI exam prep request and we reply within one business day.

Related reading: CWI requirements and career impact and how candidates fare on each exam part. Nearby and comparable CWI pages: Jacksonville, Miami, Houston and Baton Rouge.

faq.q: Is there a CWI exam prep classroom in Tampa?
faq.a: No. Atlantis has no classroom or office in Tampa. Individuals study online and send their questions to an instructor, and a Tampa Bay employer can bring the six-day course to its own site for its staff.

faq.q: How long is the Tampa CWI exam prep course?
faq.a: Six days: two on Fundamentals, one on the Part B practical, one in your Part C code book, one of timed practice papers and one of review and exam logistics. The outline is on the national CWI page.

faq.q: Does the course certify me as a CWI?
faq.a: No. The certification comes from AWS, which also runs the examination. This course gets you ready; you still apply to AWS, meet its experience and vision rules, and pass all three parts.

faq.q: Where do Tampa candidates take Parts A and C?
faq.a: At a Prometric test center. Both parts are computer-based, and you book them with the eligibility code from your AWS confirmation letter. Prometric's site shows the centers nearest Tampa.

faq.q: Where is the Part B practical held for Tampa candidates?
faq.a: AWS runs Part B at its own seminar and exam locations. When checked in November 2026, the AWS Tampa page listed no upcoming Florida seminars, so check the AWS Seminar and Exam Schedule early and expect to travel.

The AWS Florida West Coast Section. Its members sit on welding advisory boards for schools in Hillsborough, Pinellas, Manatee, Polk and Lee counties, and it posts meetings and events on sections.aws.org.

faq.q: Which code book should a Tampa ship repair welder choose?
faq.a: The CWI exam has no marine code, so AWS D1.1 is usually the closest match for hull, deck and frame steel. If your yard also does pipeline or plant piping work, API 1104 or the ASME option may suit you better.

faq.q: Can a technical college graduate in Tampa sit the CWI exam straight away?
faq.a: Usually not. AWS credits completed trade or vocational courses with one year, which still leaves four years of welding-related experience. Some graduates start with the CAWI credential, which needs less experience, then move up to CWI.

faq.q: Can a Tampa fabricator or yard have the course run on site?
faq.a: Yes. We can run all six days at your site using your own welds, gauges and code. Request a Tampa quote; we reply within one business day.

faq.q: Does Atlantis offer NDT training in Tampa as well?
faq.a: Yes. Atlantis runs ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Tampa candidates online, with practicals at the employer's facility; the employer certifies under its written practice. See NDT training in Tampa.
